card.flavorText: NZANS refers to the New Zealand Army Nursing Service, whose members served far from home during WWII. Between 1939 and 1948, 680 New Zealand nurses served in different theatres of war, while many more women served in medical and support roles through the New Zealand Women’s Army Auxiliary Corps. New Zealand nurses worked in military hospitals in the Middle East, the Pacific, and later with J Force in occupied Japan. Their duties ranged from routine ward care to treating men wounded in battle, often under difficult conditions and strict wartime censorship. In 1940, a New Zealand nurse recorded a Christmas radio message from Egypt, reassuring listeners at home that patients would still receive small gifts on Christmas morning. Some nurses experienced the danger of war directly. Matron Eva Mackay led a party of New Zealand Army nurses out of Greece and Crete in 1941 as the Allied campaign collapsed. Her group took cover during air attacks and escaped by truck and ship to the Middle East. After the war, nurses continued their service in Japan, helping care for New Zealand personnel while witnessing the early years of occupation and rebuilding.
